claims.text: Applying an SCCP processing route to a tungsten-based refractory multi-principal element alloy will simultaneously enhance room-temperature yield strength and tensile ductility.
The SCCP route produces a hierarchical microstructure that suppresses brittle fracture while maintaining high resistance to dislocation motion.
The initial tungsten-based alloy has room-temperature elongation to fracture below detection limits.
Tungsten-based refractory alloys exhibit a strength-ductility trade-off in which increasing strength tends to compromise tensile ductility.
A thermal-mechanical SCCP route can generate stepwise-controllable coherent nanoprecipitates in a tungsten-based refractory HEA.
Melting or casting can cause segregation, while conventional sintering can cause porosity and embrittlement.
HIP can induce an HCP phase associated with increased tensile brittleness.
Cr-containing tungsten refractory HEAs can form brittle Laves or other intermetallic phases that reduce mechanical performance.
Slow cooling commonly induces brittle Laves or HCP phases in refractory HEAs.
Coherent nanoprecipitates impede dislocation glide and thereby increase yield strength.
An appropriate precipitate size and distribution permits dislocation bypassing, multiplication, and cross-slip, thereby enhancing tensile ductility.
The SCCP microstructure prevents early void nucleation and catastrophic crack propagation.
The SCCP-processed alloy will simultaneously achieve a room-temperature yield strength above 2 GPa and tensile elongation above 10%.
A combination of strength above 2 GPa and ductility above 10% has previously been unattainable in this alloy family.
Standard casting, HIP, sintering, or conventional alloying generally produces either high strength with negligible ductility or high ductility with low strength.
The SCCP strategy may fail when the selected composition forms unstable or brittle phases under the processing conditions.
A processing temperature above 1800 degrees Celsius would exceed the melting point of constituent elements in NbMoTaW.
The precipitate size associated with theoretical peak strength varies by alloy system.

contradictions.description: The intervention is described as a specific thermal-mechanical processing route, but the uncertainty field states that its essential temperature, time, and cooling-rate parameters are not defined.
